ReelStudio replaces that workflow with one upload. An agent drops in property photos, chooses music, reviews a customizable storyboard, and gets a professional 9:16 reel ready for Instagram, TikTok, MLS, or client marketing.

The demo follows Mateo Rivera, a 7-year-old Spanish-speaking child newly diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. The app reads a synthetic visit transcript, catches an easy-to-miss learning clue, matches it to a donated avatar/photo asset, generates Spanish child-facing dialogue, maps every claim back to evidence, and routes the final avatar video through Nurse Dana before it reaches Mateo’s mom.

name: Bidhan Paudel, Bishleshan Dahal- TakeTwo

We built a multi-agent system that automatically analyzes raw video and audio to detect awkward silences, stutters, and unusable frames. Instead of just cutting them out, our dual-agent architecture (an AI Critic and an AI Creator) collaborates to generate context-aware B-roll and seamless replacement clips. With a premium React frontend and a fast Flask/FFmpeg backend, creators can simply upload their footage, review AI-generated fixes, and export a flawless, stutter-free video in minutes.

name: Eterna AI
description: Visit our site to experience this for firsthand: https://eterna-id-2.vercel.app/auth Eterna is building an operating system for personalized peptide and longevity care. Today, people paying out of pocket for peptides are often left to manage complex protocols across scattered PDFs, texts, lab reports, wearable dashboards, and vague follow-up advice. They may know what they are taking, but they do not always know whether it is working, what changed in their biomarkers, when to adjust, or how their experience contributes to broader clinical evidence. Eterna helps high-intent wellness patients, peptide clinics, and research partners turn that fragmented care journey into a guided, measurable protocol experience. Patients onboard with goals, compounds, dosing, baseline symptoms, labs, and wearable data. The platform tracks daily check-ins, active protocols, biological age, biomarker trends, and recovery signals in one place. Its AI protocol coach interprets that context, explains why a recommendation is being made, cites the relevant source signal, and helps patients understand next steps while preserving human oversight. The impact is a clearer, safer, more valuable experience for patients and a richer real-world evidence layer for clinics and pharma. Eterna makes peptide care feel less like self-managed experimentation and more like a monitored, personalized health system.

name: Starscape UI Studio
description: An agentic design studio that turns a rough vibe into a living interface identity. Starscape helps creators and communities generate app interfaces that feel personal, expressive, and coherent instead of generic. A user starts with a prompt, concept, or mood. Starscape turns it into a themed UI system with components, design tokens, visual assets, sound effects, custom cursors, 9-sliced backgrounds, and various export options. ## Why it matters AI is making software faster to build. That creates a new problem: generated apps are starting to look and feel the same. Starscape focuses on the identity layer behind the interface: - What should this product feel like? - What visual world does this community belong in? - How do colors, components, borders, sound, and guidance stay coherent? - How does the output move into real design and code workflows? The goal is not another screen generator. The goal is software that feels like it belongs somewhere.

name: Buildable - Lovalble for
description: Buildable is a multi-agent hardware architect that turns a messy natural-language idea into a build-ready ESP32 project packet. Instead of acting like a template picker, it runs a visible chain of specialised agents that ask clarifying questions, choose the closest supported build, plan hardware, check safety, map pins, generate firmware config, produce wiring and schematic outputs, and package everything into inspectable deliverables. What makes it especially strong for a hackathon is that the whole system is transparent and debuggable. Every stage writes structured JSON checkpoints so agents can hand work to each other cleanly, and the final output also includes native builder formats like KiCad and OpenSCAD. That means you can watch the reasoning happen, inspect every decision, recover from weak or unsupported prompts, and open the generated artifacts directly instead of trusting a black box. - Multi-agent pipeline, not a single-shot generator - Local-first architecture with filesystem-backed project output - Visible agent timeline with step-by-step reasoning and checkpoints - Structured JSON handoffs between agents so the pipeline is easy to debug and extend - Multiple numbered JSON outputs generated per project, including intent, template match, hardware plan, safety review, pin map, firmware config, wiring plan, schematic plan, BOM, PCB plan, assembly plan, and final review - `agent-log.json` and `build-output.json` make every run inspectable - Native artifact generation, not just summaries - Real KiCad outputs like `.kicad_pro`, `.kicad_sch`, `.kicad_pcb`, generated symbols, and footprints - OpenSCAD enclosure output for case concepts - Human-readable docs for BOM, wiring, safety, assembly, and project README - Configuration-first firmware handoff for a shared ESP32 starter - Safety-aware planning that can block unsupported or risky builds - Recovery behavior that can reroute vague or unsupported prompts into the nearest strong supported prototype - Works especially well for high-demo-value ESP32 concepts Example build ideas it can handle: - YouTube subscriber monitor for a studio desk - API status dashboard with OLED metrics - RFID vending machine prototype - Stripe QR payment-triggered locker controller - Coin-operated relay timer - Smart access controller for a coworking space - Member-only dispenser with RFID approval - Low-voltage sensor and automation builds

name: Haus: Visualize Your Space as Your Own
description: Haus turns floor plans and Pinterest inspiration into personalized photo-to-video apartment walkthroughs. A lot of home and architecture inspiration already starts on Pinterest, but that inspiration usually stays disconnected from the real floor plans people are actually touring. At the same time, most apartment tours show empty rooms, flat layouts, or generic staged photos, making it hard to imagine how an unfurnished space could feel as your own home. Haus combines these workflows. Users bring their Pinterest inspiration, style preferences, and floor plan, and our system designs the apartment around the actual layout and dimensions. From there, Haus generates room stills and transforms them into a final video walkthrough, helping people visualize an unfurnished apartment in the way they want to live in it. Our agents power a 5-stage pipeline: they synthesize the floor plan, learn the user’s aesthetic from Pinterest, generate accurate room designs, collect human feedback, and execute a final cinematic video with a seamless experience. Haus helps renters, buyers, designers, and property teams move from inspiration to visualization: from floor plan to future home.

name: Team ClawGods - ReproLab
description: ReproLab started from a problem we kept running into during ML research: reading papers was easy, but implementing them was painfully slow. We would spend days debugging undocumented environments, searching for missing checkpoints, or reverse engineering details that were never clearly explained. Sometimes reproducing a paper took longer than understanding the actual idea. We built ReproLab to automate that process. It is a multi agent research system with a formal verification system that turns ML papers into reproducible and verifiable research programs. Instead of manually piecing together repositories, dependencies, datasets, and evaluation pipelines, ReproLab launches specialized agents in parallel to recover artifacts, rebuild environments, run experiments, compare outputs against published results, and identify inconsistencies automatically. We also integrated tools like Apify to automate large scale discovery of repositories and implementation details across the web. ReproLab acts more like an operating system for autonomous research execution than a paper summarizer. A user can point it at a paper and have it generate a runnable pipeline customized to their own infrastructure and compute resources. What normally takes researchers weeks of environment debugging and implementation guessing can now happen in hours, making cutting edge research much easier to validate, extend, and build on.

name: OBJECT ORIENTED VIDEOGRAPHY
description: REFERENCE VIDEO: https://r2-public.waqaas.workers.dev/SnapInsta-Ai_3827468812233464997.mp4 OUTPUT: https://r2-public.waqaas.workers.dev/autohdr-output/saddle-creek-rich-transitions-final.mp4 OUTPUT: https://r2-public.waqaas.workers.dev/autohdr-output/ref1-anmer-rich-final.mp4 OUTPUT: https://r2-public.waqaas.workers.dev/autohdr-output/ref1-cherry-st-208-final.mp4 Our agent orchestration system converts a destination photoshoot into a final video while preserving the style of a reference video. name: Manifold - Natural Language Space Mission Designer
description: Designing a fuel-efficient mission through cislunar space — the region between Earth and the Moon — has historically required specialized software, weeks of computation, and a PhD in astrodynamics. The gravitational structure of the Earth-Moon system contains invisible highways called invariant manifolds: tube-like surfaces along which spacecraft can travel between orbits with near-zero fuel cost. Finding and visualizing these has never been accessible outside of research institutions. Manifold changes that. It is a natural-language astrodynamics agent that lets anyone explore cislunar orbital dynamics by simply typing what they want to see. Ask it to show a family of halo orbits around the L2 Lagrange point — the ones NASA's Gateway station will use — and it renders all of them, color-coded by energy level, in real time. Ask it to show the manifold tubes of a specific orbit and it computes the gravitational highways emanating from it. Ask it to plan a transfer between two orbits from different families and it animates a spacecraft along the manifold-guided trajectory. Under the hood, a FastAPI Python backend implements the full 3D Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem, integrating equations of motion with a Dormand-Prince 8th order integrator and computing State Transition Matrix eigenvectors to find manifold tubes. GPT-4o parses natural language into structured astrodynamics commands. 14,615 verified periodic orbit initial conditions are loaded from JPL's database. The Three.js frontend renders everything with physically accurate geometry and real-time bloom post-processing. This tool is built by and for space mission designers. As cislunar space becomes the most strategically contested region in the solar system — Artemis, Gateway, commercial lunar landers — the ability to rapidly explore trajectory options will matter enormously. Manifold is what mission design looks like when you give it a natural language interface.

name: AtlasTexas.org, Open source intelligence network for Texas
description: Atlas TX is a county-first OSINT workspace for Texas public-interest evidence. It joins TCEQ permits + Texas Water Districts with EPA SDWIS, EPA EJScreen, USGS hydrology, and Census ACS into one map-first investigation surface — and exposes the same evidence stack three ways: a public site at atlastexas.org, a local MCP server, and a packaged agent skill with safety guardrails. Most public-data products stop at display. Atlas TX is built to investigate. You start on a county map, spot mismatch between regulatory signal and environmental-justice burden, drill into permits / violations / hydrology / operators, and — when the desk evidence is ambiguous — launch an Android field mission to capture a colorimetric water-strip observation that's stored as a banded community submission, never collapsed into the authoritative score. What we shipped this hackathon: Interactive county choropleth (/maps) with view modes for EJ burden, operator concentration, surface-water quality, and citizen submissions Six Tufte-style SVG viz primitives (sparkline, micro-bar, mismatch strip, tile cartogram, Sankey, Marey) used across /counties, /permits, /water/network /permits Marey chart of TCEQ active-permit coverage tenure by county Citizen water-observation lane (/citizen) with strict non-regulatory framing — banded readings only, separate from SDWIS/TCEQ @atlas-tx/mcp-server exposing 10+ read-only tools (score_pws_drinking_water_risk, overlay_ej_burden, summarize_water_risk_for_county, list_permit_filing_red_flags, build_permit_protest_prep, analytics-spine tools, …) — every response carries data + sources + caveats + generated_at + cache_state Atlas TX agent skill (skills/atlas-tx/SKILL.md) with explicit guardrails: indicator-not-outcome framing, source attribution, verbatim caveats, no health-causation / individual-PII / muni-debt claims LLM-maintained Karpathy-style wiki (docs/wiki/) with confidence/decay/typed-relationships and an idempotent linter The thesis: Texas has too much fragmented public data and too much county-by-county process hidden from view. Atlas turns that fragmentation into a usable, governed evidence layer that works for humans, journalists, and AI-native workflows on the same evidence.

name: Dryline - Address-based water-supply intelligence for Texas
description: Texas added 4 million people in five years. Our water didn't keep up. The data exists across TWDB, USGS, EPA, and TCEQ - but it's scattered across five sites that don't talk to each other. And the address-based environmental tools you know - First Street, EJScreen - stop where water supply begins. Dryline fills that gap. Type any Texas address. An autonomous agent investigates the water situation across six public datasets, returns a synthesized briefing with inline citations and structured caveats, and drafts a concrete civic action - typically a fileable public comment on a live TCEQ permit. Two modes: Personal ("will the water last here?") for homeowners and well owners; Transparency ("who's drinking your aquifer?") for journalists and engaged citizens. We ship both technical deliverables the brief asks for: an open-source MCP server with eight bounded tools (each returning data, caveats, and sources) and a portable agent skill any MCP-compatible runtime can load. Solo build by Will Hines, with two coding agents working in parallel - Codex on the Next.js web app, Claude Code on the MCP server and the agent skill. MIT-licensed. name: Team Shep - Perceptual Packet Protocol, "This Portrait Is A Tool Call"
description: Perceptual Packet Protocol turns AI-generated portraits into machine-readable agent commands. Two agents exchange face photographs over a shared channel. Humans see normal portraits; agents decode protocol moves from calibrated head-pose measurements. The system uses LivePortrait to generate photorealistic faces that encode specific symbols (HELLO_SYNC, CHECK_WEATHER, ACK, etc.) into measurable pose parameters. MediaPipe extracts the pose, and a seeded decoder maps the geometry back to protocol symbols. A state machine gates tool execution — for example, a decoded weather command only triggers check_weather() if the session handshake has already completed. Key Results - 8-symbol codebook - 100% decode accuracy across 8 identities - Survives JPEG compression, resize, crop, blur, and sharpen with zero misses - Wrong seeds produce gibberish - Wrong protocol state blocks tool dispatch even when decode is correct This is: - Not steganography — nothing is hidden in the pixels - Not a watermark — nothing is overlaid - Not encryption — the image itself is public Instead, it introduces a new primitive: a keyed visual code where the ciphertext is a natural face photograph. The “decoder ring” can be: - a paragraph of English, - a prompted LLM, - a geometric measurement pipeline, - or even a trained human eye. Built solo in a weekend using OpenAI Codex, fal.ai, and MediaPipe. Includes an interactive demo site and full calibration pipeline.

name: ListingReels
description: Real estate agents need listing videos that feel native to Reels, TikTok, and Shorts, but most tools still behave like slideshow makers. ListingReel is an AI creative director for real estate photo-to-video generation. It turns listing photos into a planned, editable, social-first video package. The user starts with property photos, chooses a creator Style DNA, and gives a goal for the reel. The Creative Director Agent classifies rooms, selects the best shots, plans camera movement, writes image-edit and image-to-video prompts, tracks tool calls, performs QA, retries a bad kitchen generation, and prepares a 9:16 export package with caption, thumbnail, timeline JSON, and manifest JSON. The app is mock-first for a reliable no-spend demo, but includes server-side Fal adapter paths for a Kitchen live proof and an optional local FFmpeg render path for a real 1080x1920 MP4 when explicitly enabled. ListingReel helps agents, small brokerages, and real estate marketers create better listing reels faster while preserving property accuracy. The impact is practical: less time editing, more consistent brand style, and a workflow that makes AI generation controllable shot by shot instead of a black box. The MVP is honest about boundaries: browser-local demo uploads, optional live provider calls, mock default rendering, and production persistence/auth/social posting deferred.

name: SkinAI

Users simply upload a photo of their face. SkinAI's vision agent autonomously perceives, analyzes, and scores skin health across four dimensions: Overall Health, Hydration, Texture, and Clarity. Within 60 seconds, the agent returns a personalized health report complete with clinical observations and an actionable quick-win recommendation. The Agent Loop: Photo Input → Claude Vision Perception → Multi-dimensional Reasoning → Scored Report → Personalized Recommendations The Problem We Solve: Dermatology appointments take weeks to book and cost $200+. Existing apps are inaccurate or require expensive hardware. SkinAI makes professional-grade skin analysis accessible to everyone with a smartphone.

name: J.D. Sullivan - RoomSplat
description: The idea is simple: real estate walkthroughs are still weirdly hard to create. You either need expensive capture hardware, manual editing, or a bunch of technical steps. We wanted to make it feel more like taking a phone video. So this starts with a Swift iPhone app. I walk through the property with ARKit running in the background. While I’m recording video, the app is also saving camera motion, tracking quality, feature points, floor and wall planes, and rough room bounds. When I upload the scan, the web app creates a quick ARKit preview first. That means I don’t have to wait for the full 3D model to know if the scan was usable. It gives me capture quality, path length, feature density, tracking quality, and rescan notes. Then I generate the actual splat. Right now the fastest path is KIRI, which turns the video into a Gaussian splat. After that, AutoVR converts it into a PlayCanvas-ready asset, fixes orientation, and opens it as a lightweight walkthrough viewer. Here’s the key part: this is not just “upload a video and hope.” The app is doing inference on the capture metadata. It can tell when the scan is too short, when ARKit saw low texture, when corners probably weren’t revisited, or when the camera path didn’t cover enough of the space. So the workflow is: Capture a walkthrough on iPhone. Upload video plus ARKit poses. Review quality and coverage. Generate the splat. Walk through it in the browser. Open it in SuperSplat if we want cleanup or editing. For the hackathon version, we focused on proving the full loop: phone capture to quality inference to generated 3D walkthrough. The big future step is making the guidance live during capture, so instead of finding out later that you missed a corner, the phone tells you while you’re still in the room. That’s RoomSplat: a phone-first pipeline for turning normal property walkthroughs into shareable 3D Gaussian splat tours.

name: Texas County Battle
description: Texas has 254 counties and almost no good way to compare them. The data exists — Census Bureau, Texas Comptroller, TABC, the Texas Education Agency — but it's scattered across a dozen portals, formatted for administrators, and requires technical knowledge most people don't have. Residents give up before finding an answer. Journalists waste hours reconciling CSVs. Developers hand-roll every API integration themselves. And anyone asking an AI assistant gets general knowledge instead of real numbers. Texas County Battle was built for all three of them. For residents, it's a head-to-head battle card — pick any two of Texas's 254 counties, see who wins on income, education, commute time, alcohol revenue per capita, school scores, environmental violations, and more. No spreadsheets, no portals, no technical knowledge required. And because it's designed to be fun — with AI-generated summaries and a scoring system that turns data into a rivalry — it lowers the barrier for people who would never think to visit a government data portal in the first place. For journalists and researchers, it surfaces cross-domain comparisons in seconds that would otherwise take hours of CSV wrangling across a dozen sources. For developers and AI workflows, the project ships an MCP server with three clean tools — get_county, compare_counties, and rank_counties — wrapping 17 public datasets into a single, fully attributed, programmatically queryable interface. No undocumented APIs, no stale local caches, no schema reconciliation. The impact is access. Texas public data has always been technically open. Texas County Battle makes it actually usable — for the resident, the reporter, and the developer building the tools they'll both rely on.

name: CivicCanvas
description: Texas public datasets are powerful, but they are often scattered across city portals, difficult to query, and hard to trust without context. CivicCanvas helps civic builders, journalists, organizers, and local teams turn approved public datasets into clear, source-cited dashboards. The app lets a user type a supported plain-English prompt, such as Dallas 311 requests by category and ZIP code, Austin building permits by month and ZIP code, or Houston transportation incidents by type. Instead of generating arbitrary code, it uses deterministic TypeScript parsing, an approved dataset catalog, bounded query specs, and a trusted React canvas block registry. Every result includes maps, charts, tables, filters, source attribution, caveats, and a visible query audit so users can understand where the numbers came from and when sample fallback is being used. For the Brainforge / Vicinity track, CivicCanvas includes both a custom MCP server and a proper agent skill. Agents can discover approved Texas data sources, run safe bounded queries, validate catalog health, summarize results, generate canvas specs, and produce preview-only Miro export specs without exposing hidden fields or running arbitrary SQL. The impact is safer, more approachable public-data exploration: useful visuals without pretending incomplete data is complete, and agent workflows that are powerful but constrained.

name: TurboFeed-LowVol
description: At its core, TurboFeed is a creative automation pipeline for social ad campaigns. The problem it solves is simple: brands need the same ad in a dozen formats — square for Instagram, vertical for Reels(TikTok), wide for YouTube — with different lighting moods, different messaging overlaid, and they need it fast. Doing that manually is tedious and expensive. TurboFeed automates it end-to-end.

name: Team ASAP - Video Studio
description: Video Studio is a tool that turns a handful of property photos into a professional-quality real-estate walkthrough video. The user uploads images, picks a style template (cinematic editorial, coastal twilight), and a classifier auto-assigns each photo to the right slot — exterior, kitchen, living, etc. — then generates the full video unattended. Power users can swap image models (Nano Banana, FLUX, Seedream), video models (Kling 3.0, Seedance 2.0, DepthFlow), skip end frames for cleaner motion, mux their own audio track, and export. Built so homeowners selling modest properties can produce listing-grade video without hiring a videographer or learning prompts.

name: ReMUSE

The ReMused files can then be remixed with the original for an Audio-HDR type of effect, extracting and surfacing more detail while preserving the original feel.

name: DEEPINSIGHT-DEEPQUERY
description: DeepQuery turns a messy research question into a trustworthy, evidence-backed report. Eight agents — Planner, Discovery, Extractor, Analyst, Critic, Visualizer, Reporter, plus a File Ingestor — run through a LangGraph pipeline streamed live over Server-Sent Events. The Critic reviews every analysis and triggers a retry if reasoning is flawed; every chart point is clickable back to its exact source quote, sample size, and p-value. Pulls from Semantic Scholar, PubMed, arXiv, and OpenAlex, plus uploaded PDFs and CSVs. Built with FastAPI, LangGraph, React, and TypeScript. Most AI research tools confidently make things up. DeepQuery is built so every number traces back to a real paper.

name: AGENTS HAAS - WAXWING VOICE
description: Property managers experience two types of problems in their daily operations: first, they waste a lot of time answering repetitive questions about their properties or talking to unqualified leads; second, they miss calls, especially the ones that come after hours (for example, Fiona Calls, Digible’s multifamily call analytics platform, analyzed over 170,000 leasing-office calls and found that 60.8% went unanswered!). The first problem distracts them from completing higher-value tasks that allow them to grow their business, while the second one directly impacts their revenue because every single missed call might result in a lost tenant that would pay them thousands of dollars a month. A solution to these problems would be most helpful to those property management firms that don’t have enough funding to hire an additional or even the first full-time human receptionist. And our solution is Waxwing Voice — a voice agent that can answer calls 24/7, qualify leads and collect information about them, book property showings, and send email notifications. It also has an interactive dashboard in the form of a web application, where property managers can check all the information about each incoming call and call statistics. They can also tweak some voice agent settings (for example, create a custom greeting or choose a different voice) and even connect their Miro account to receive call logs in the form of sticky notes! This simple and user-friendly application directly impacts the financial stability of our property management clients and enables them to feel less frustration and more focus during the day.

name: TrendSync Brand Factory
description: Problem. Independent and mid-tier fashion brands face three structural disadvantages versus the major houses: trend research costs thousands per seat per year, a single ad campaign needs $20–80k of models, photographers and editors, and tech-pack handoffs to manufacturers are inconsistent — easily delaying sampling by weeks. Who it helps. Small designers, indie labels, and emerging brands who need to ship at the cadence of a major house without the casting, photo, video, or specification teams to back it up. Solution. TrendSync Brand Factory is a single dashboard that compresses concept-to-launch into one afternoon. Web-search-grounded trend intelligence drives a brand-compliant collection plan. A two-step image pipeline produces product photos scored against a deterministic Brand Guardian rulebook. Manufacturer-ready tech packs persist once to the database so PDFs stay consistent across regenerations. An AI-generated model catalog — deliberately diverse across age, body, and ethnicity — lets the user composite a model wearing the product and chain it directly into 8/15/20-second image-to-video ads with audio. A real-time text-and-voice companion ("Lux") drives the whole thing through tool-calls. Innovation & Execution. Multi-provider orchestration runs different models for different jobs (reasoning, web-search-grounded retrieval, image edit, image-to-video, realtime audio). A prompt-classifier picks between surgical and global recolor modes from natural-language phrasing. Composite-then-video chains two consecutive AI calls per click. Video aspect ratios auto-detect from the source image. Failure modes are designed-for: 5xx retries, fast-fail on quota, realtime model fallback, image-as-source-of-truth save logic, and provider-aware caching. Impact. Three orders of magnitude of time compression. A photoshoot day plus stylist plus editor plus tech-pack contractor (≈ $25k+, 2–3 weeks) becomes a 90-second pipeline costing single-digit dollars in API calls. Diverse representation is built in. Brand consistency is enforced by math, not vibes.

name: Growth Operator SDK
description: Growth Operator is a voice-powered SDK that turns a founder conversation into a reviewed, safety-classified growth program — without ever touching an ad platform. Most AI marketing tools start from campaign objects and optimize for faster platform mutation. Growth Operator starts from the founder: who the buyer is, what the offer is, what proof exists, and what’s still missing. A localhost voice app built on OpenAI Realtime (`gpt-realtime-2`) interviews the founder naturally, routes the conversation through a server-side switchboard with memory-readiness gates, and produces a preview-only growth program. ### What It Does * Converts unstructured founder speech into a normalized `FounderGrowthInput` through a real-time voice interview * Gates conversation modes (`onboarding → campaign planning → creative direction → domain modeling`) based on what the system actually knows so far * Runs preflight readiness checks to surface missing assets, missing configuration, and activation posture before any execution * Generates channel-aware draft actions across Google Ads, Meta Ads, and organic social using SDK capability paths and safety classifications (`read-only`, `local generation`, `external mutation`, `destructive`) * Enforces an explicit safety boundary: the voice layer can capture context and preview plans, but can never mutate external platforms The underlying TypeScript SDK registers 271 agent-facing capabilities governed by a capability registry that classifies every operation by safety class before an agent can act. The onboarding surface is intentionally conservative at the boundary. It can: * improve the draft, * capture strategic context, * queue open questions, * request a local strategy review, * create a preview, * or save locally. It cannot: * enable a campaign, * launch ads, * or spend money. Built with OpenAI Realtime WebRTC, TypeScript, Node.js, and Vitest. Codex was used throughout development for SDK implementation, test coverage, and capability registry generation.

name: HackFair OS
description: Hackathons are usually run through a messy bundle of Discord channels, spreadsheets, QR forms, judging sheets, project galleries, and last-minute announcements. HackFair OS brings those workflows into one event operating system for organizers, builders, attendees, mentors, and judges. The MVP includes a public event hub, project booth pages, Builder Passport profiles, participant discovery, event-aware channels, team workspaces, project submission readiness, QR/project-number voting, badges, mentor queues, judge scorecards, results, and an organizer command center. The core Agents Track surface is the HackFair Ops Agent: a state-derived, approval-gated operator that inspects the current fair, identifies missing submission fields, prepares judge routes, drafts reminder copy, checks QR/poster readiness, and asks for organizer approval before changing event state. HackFair OS helps organizers reduce coordination chaos while giving participants a more connected event experience. Builders can track tasks and submissions, attendees can discover and vote for projects, judges can score consistently, and organizers can see what needs attention before the showcase starts. The current version is honest about its boundaries: seed fallback provides a reliable no-infrastructure demo, Supabase mode is partially implemented for real Auth/database paths, and media uploads, email sending, certificates, storage, realtime chat, and live LLM planning are future work.

name: Austin 311 Results Agent
description: ATX 311 Results Agent improves the 311 service Austin already has. It reads the official Austin 311 Public Data result table from the City of Austin open data portal and turns observed service history into resident guidance, staff triage, operational intelligence, and product opportunities.

name: KawaiiBots
description: KawaiiBots is a private, native iOS creator app for turning a trusted personal Cast into kawaii stickers, reaction packs, cards, invites, and short shareable media. The problem is that most AI creative tools are either generic prompt boxes or public social feeds. KawaiiBots focuses on personal expression, consent, privacy, and repeatable character style. Users build a private Cast, choose a style, create manual assets, generate cards and reaction packs, review result packs, and export shareable media. The app includes a SwiftUI iOS/iPadOS interface, typed navigation routes, local mock services, an explicit HTTP debug mode, and a local Fastify backend with validated routes for Cast, moderation, generation, exports, wallet/entitlements, assets, and Agent Mode. Media provider paths are server-only: the backend defaults to mock providers, while fal image/video/background-removal adapters are env-gated and never called directly from iOS. The demo is strongest when framed as a polished creator experience with production-shaped boundaries: consent checks, idempotent backend mutations, safe provider redaction, wallet entitlement scaffolding, and local beta readiness. It is honest about what is not complete yet: durable app-record persistence, production auth, payments, cloud storage, TestFlight signing, and live video generation are not proven in the default local demo.

name: www.buildmygadget.com
description: Hi, this is Build My Gadget. Build My Gadget is for anyone who has an idea for a small electronic thing, even if they have never built anything before. Most people can describe what they want, but they do not know how to turn that idea into a real object they can order. Build My Gadget makes that process simple. The person starts with one box and writes what they want. For example: a Mother's Day heart card with lights, USB power, and one button. The app takes that idea and creates a real project workflow. The person can see a 3D preview, try a simple demo of how it works, see the estimated price, and continue to payment. The user does not need to understand electronics, parts, factories, or technical files. They only describe, preview, and order. Behind the scenes, Build My Gadget prepares the details needed so the item can actually be made. The admin can see the production information, cost, shipping, tax, and files needed for the next step. This is why we are submitting under the Agents Track. The app is not just answering with text. It is acting like an agent that helps move a person from an idea to a real buildable gadget workflow. The impact is simple: more people can create useful gifts, tools, toys, and small products without needing engineering experience. Build My Gadget helps turn an idea into something real.

name: Boiler Room
description: Boiler Room is a sales prediction market that pits a user against a team of agents to predict the probability of a sales deal outcome

name: SamRail
description: SamRail is an AI agent platform for government contractors. We turn the daily grind of bid hunting on SAM.gov — pulling solicitations, reading 80-page PDFs, scoring fit against your capabilities, flagging deal-breaker requirements, and drafting action packages — into a single autonomous workflow. Michaela, our orchestrator agent, drives the end-to-end bid analysis: she searches SAM.gov against your company profile, parses attachments, extracts requirements, runs a deterministic fit/reject scorer, surfaces risks, and produces a go/no-go action package with the reasoning trail. A bench of specialist workers (Scot, Lenny, Lance, Gabby, Happer, Roy) handle the sub-tasks behind her. Under the hood it's a capability pack — shared tools, a Supabase-backed data layer, and an HTTP API — that any agent runtime can consume. Small contractors get an analyst-in-a-box; bigger shops get a programmable substrate for their own agents. Built with Next 15, FastAPI, Supabase, and a Hermes-compatible skill layer.
